hints: You only ever need the one or two values in the middle. What would let you see both sides of the middle at once?
Two heaps: a max-heap for the smaller half and a min-heap for the larger half.
Route each sample by comparing it with the max-heap's top, then move one top across if the sizes differ by more than one; read the median from the tops.

signals: States the sort-per-read baseline and why interleaved reads make it costly
Uses a max-heap for the low half and a min-heap for the high half
Keeps the invariant: every low value is at most every high value, sizes differ by at most one
Gives O(log n) per add and O(1) per median
Handles the even case by averaging the two tops
